messages:
Ava: Morning — async standup. What I did: finished the baseline prompt-set normalization for synthia-v2 (es/en), kicked off evals against the regression suite, and pushed PR #482 with a small prompt-cleaner (normalizes whitespace, removes trailing tokens). Blockers: quantized tinyq variant shows heavy repetition on long prefixes (>512). Need someone to sanity-check KV warmup and a quick CR on PR #482. pinging @Devon for review. Example failing snippet below. 

Ava: Failing case (short):
```
> prompt: "Translate: La economía creció un 2% en el último trimestre..."
model output: "La economía creció un 2% en el último trimestre, la economía creció... la economía creció..."
```

Ava: Eval command I ran: `rw-eval run --model synthia-v2-tinyq --prompts prompts/intl/es-train.jsonl --max-tokens 256 --metrics bleu,replication_rate` — replication_rate jumped from 0.03 to 0.28 on quantized.

Devon: On review queue, will look after standup. Quick question: did you run with the KV-cache warmup flag? infra rolled a warmup tweak yesterday that may affect tinyq. If not, try `--kv-warmup 1` and repro. Also FYI: I saw a spike in 95p token latency in us-west for tinyq yesterday around 03:10 UTC.

Ava: Hey — I did not set `--kv-warmup`, will re-run. Reproduced locally with `--kv-warmup 0` consistently. With `--kv-warmup 1` I see less repetition but still higher than fp16 baseline. Linking PR and logs: https://git.redwood/PR/482 and https://observability/redwood/logs/trace/abc123

Priya: What's the user impact here? Any customers on Dedicated using tinyq? If it's a small perf/regression we can gate rollout.

Ava: Minimal customer-facing impact yet — only internal perf tests and a small POC team. But if we push tinyq to Dedicated pools it could affect some internal SLAs. My plan: block rollout for tinyq until we pin cause or add a fallback.

observability-bot: Alert: synthia-v2-tinyq — 95p token latency +120% in us-west over baseline in the last 24h. Related traces: https://observability/redwood/trace/abc123.

Luca: Recommend immediate rollout safety: add a canary with traffic=5% and automatic fallback to synthia-v2-fp16 if replication_rate > 0.15 for 10m. Example rollout snippet (pseudo-config):
```
rollout_policy:
  canary: 0.05
  check: replication_rate > 0.15 for 10m -> fallback: synthia-v2-fp16
```
I'll add a short PR to console to wire the check as an emergency guard.

Devon: I'll take the PR review for Ava's prompt-cleaner and also look into kernel selection paths that touch quantized KV. If anyone can drop one or two failing prompts into this thread I can run `rw-replay` locally against different kernel profiles.

Ava: Dropping two failing prompts below (sanitized):
- "Situación: el mercado muestra señales de..."
- "Informe: El PIB aumentó..."

Ava: Next steps for today: 1) re-run evals with `--kv-warmup 1` and attach traces, 2) @Devon review PR #482, 3) @Luca to open guard PR for rollout, 4) hold tinyq Dedicated rollout. Will post results by EOD PST.

Devon: Sounds good — I'll aim to review PR + run replays by 1800 PT.

Priya: Thanks team — keep me posted if we need to pause any customer-facing experiments.

Luca: I'll draft the emergency guard and post a small changelog entry in #eng-releases when ready. :thumbsup: 

Ava: Thanks all — tagging this as resolved for now until re-run. :white_check_mark:
